I have a business. Is my bookkeeping ready for tax season?

Answer seven simple yes-or-no questions. You will get a clear score and a short list of exactly what to fix — so tax time is calm, not a scramble.

By JK Accounting Group · For business owners in the US

Built with JuliaFounder · speaks your language

Answer these seven questions

Just say yes or no. Nothing is saved and no email is needed.

1. Do you have a separate bank account just for your business?

Not mixed together with your personal money.

2. Are your business records up to date within the last month?

3. Do you keep your receipts and bills, on paper or on your computer?

4. Is every business cost sorted into a type (like rent, supplies, travel)?

5. Do your records match your bank statements each month?

This is called reconciling — checking your books against the bank.

6. Did you file last year's taxes on time?

7. Do you know your profit for this year so far?

Answer all seven to see your score.

Your result

    Get your books ready — book a free call → A 20‑minute call. No cost, no pressure.

Why this matters

In plain words, so tax time never catches you out.

  • Good books save you money. When every cost is recorded, you claim everything you are allowed to — and pay less tax. Messy books mean missed deductions.
  • They keep you safe. If the IRS ever asks a question, clean records are your answer. They also matter if you ever apply for a loan.
  • They make tax time calm. When the books are ready all year, there is no last-minute rush and no surprise. That is the whole point of doing it as you go.
